items.title: Fading Cobalt Rally Is Testing Congo’s Efforts to Control Prices
items.description: Cobalt’s spectacular rally is reversing as the Democratic Republic of Congo’s exports of the battery metal pick up under a strict new regime, testing the top producer’s efforts to control prices.

items.title: RBNZ More Likely To Wait Until December to Hike, Silk Says
items.description: New Zealand’s central bank is more likely to wait until December before raising interest rates again, according to Assistant Governor Karen Silk.

items.title: Philippine Inflation Eases to 6.1% After Successive Rate Hikes
items.description: Philippine inflation eased for the fourth straight month in August while staying above the central bank’s target, on slower increases in utility rates and food prices.

items.title: Carry Trade Exodus Fuels Yen Surge Ahead of BOJ Rate Decision
items.description: A rush to unwind yen-funded carry trades helped send the currency to a one-month high against the dollar as traders ramped up bets on further Bank of Japan rate hikes.

items.title: Australian Property Developer Bathla Survives, For Now
items.description: Australia's Bathla Group remains in discussions over a short-term funding deal that would avert the collapse of one of Sydney’s largest residential property developers. Bloomberg's Paul Allen reports.

items.title: US Dollar Slumps to Start September as Yen Surges on Rate Bets
items.description: The dollar slumped to start September as traders cut bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike this month and a surging yen rippled across global currency markets.

items.title: Gold to End Volatile Week Higher as Fedspeak Trims Rate-Hike Bet
items.description: Gold steadied — after rising more than 2% on Thursday — after a Federal Reserve official’s comments on inflation helped to lower the odds of an interest-rate hike.

items.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Exports Fell in August on Weak Indian Demand
items.description: Malaysian palm oil exports likely fell last month on weaker-than-usual festival demand in major buyer India.

items.title: Yen’s $103 Billion Short Risks Unwind Below 155, JPMorgan Says
items.description: A further unwind of sizable short positions could accelerate the yen’s gains if it strengthens past 155 per dollar, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co. strategists.

items.title: Pacific Leaders Criticize China’s Recent Ballistic Missile Test
items.description: The leaders of Pacific island nations criticized China’s recent missile test in their region, an unexpected move after earlier failed attempts to agree on a response.

items.title: Hong Kong’s Picky IPO Issuers Rewrite Playbook for Allocations
items.description: Hong Kong’s boom in initial public offerings has turned getting shares in the hottest deals into something of an invitation-only affair.

items.title: Stocks Rise as Fed Rate-Hike Bets Ease, Yen Gains: Markets Wrap
items.description: Asian stocks and currencies rose as investors pared bets on a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this month, weakening the dollar. The yen strengthened.

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 4
items.description: Oil headed for its biggest weekly gain since July as renewed US-Iran hostilities heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: India’s SEBI to Review Options Settlement Pricing After Closing Auction Chaos
items.description: India’s markets regulator may propose changes to equity derivatives settlement pricing after feedback that the new closing-auction system triggered sharp price swings.
